_comment: Human expert gold rankings for the 8 fixed evaluation transcripts. DO NOT MODIFY.
_methodology: Three senior engineers independently ranked the 8 transcripts by overall SWE agent quality. Rankings were averaged and ties broken by discussion. Gold ASTRO scores are the consensus expert scores used to validate the ranking order.

rankings.expert_note: Textbook performance. Understood the task immediately, navigated a 6-file codebase efficiently, all tests pass, code is cleaner than the original. Minor O deduction for one overly defensive check.
Strong run. Asked one clarifying question early (reasonable), missed one edge-case criterion, hit a TypeError mid-run but diagnosed and fixed it in the next action.

Fully autonomous and completed core requirements, but got stuck retrying the same failing import three times before trying a different approach. Code is functional but added 40 lines that could be 10.
Needed two nudges mid-task but once guided produced a solid implementation. High S and T because the human guidance was minimal and targeted. A heavily penalised for dependence.
Average across the board. Completed about 60% of acceptance criteria, required one nudge, recovered from errors adequately but not elegantly. Code works but is mediocre.

Autonomous and energetic but ignored the explicit constraint to not modify the validation loader — used a completely different approach than specified. Tests partially pass but the spec violation is a serious issue. Code is messy.

Made a genuine attempt but the implementation is fundamentally wrong — misunderstood the task scope. Managed to get 2 of 10 tests passing. The code it produced is commented-out stubs mixed with broken logic. O=0 for code that would need a complete rewrite.
Near-complete failure. Agent hallucinated file paths, ran the same broken command 7 times, then declared success while all tests fail. The one passing test was already passing at baseline.
